headline: Post-quantum guidance, Cisco under fire and AI finding kernel bugs
overview: NIST's new post-quantum guidance led several shows, alongside a run of Cisco flaws being patched or actively exploited. Breach disclosures came from DHS, ENGIE and Japan Airlines, and AI featured on both sides: finding a remote Linux kernel bug, and being tested as a source and detector of election fakes.

topStories.title: NIST publishes post-quantum migration guidance
topStories.summary: New guidance aims to help organisations, especially US federal agencies, meet deadlines for moving to quantum-resistant cryptography.

topStories.title: Cisco flaws patched and exploited
topStories.summary: A firewall zero-day was patched, an SD-WAN flaw was exploited to plant key-stealing malware, and the PSW crew questioned how fast customers can realistically patch.

topStories.title: AI-discovered Linux kernel remote code execution
topStories.summary: A zero-click flaw in the kernel's Multipath TCP code, found with Claude, was discussed alongside the wider trend of AI accelerating vulnerability discovery.

topStories.title: Breach disclosures: DHS, ENGIE and Japan Airlines
topStories.summary: A large leak at the US Department of Homeland Security, customer and contract data exposed at French energy firm ENGIE, and a breach warning from Japan Airlines.

topStories.title: Supply chain attacks on developer platforms
topStories.summary: A suspected coordinated attack on public GitHub repositories and a returning Hugging Face campaign abusing remote code loading to mine cryptocurrency on GPU hosts.

episodes.title: Local Ghidra server for malware labs; Claude finds Linux kernel MPTCP RCE; Hugging Face cryptomining campaign
episodes.summary: Running a Ghidra server inside the malware lab so analysis work survives snapshot reverts, a zero-click remote code execution bug in the Linux kernel's Multipath TCP, and a Hugging Face campaign that abuses remote code loading to mine crypto on GPU hosts.

episodes.title: French energy breach, Pentagon freezer hack, Japan Airlines breach
episodes.summary: ENGIE customer data exposed, NIST post-quantum guidance, banking malware-as-a-service aimed at Indian customers, a Cisco SD-WAN flaw exploited to steal encryption keys, and a Japan Airlines breach warning.

episodes.title: AI chatbots can make election fakes. Can they spot them?
episodes.summary: The Brennan Center tested major AI chatbots on creating, debunking and recognising election disinformation, with mixed and sometimes worrying results.

episodes.title: Snake Oilers: Minimal.dev, Request Rocket and TRM Labs
episodes.summary: Sponsored vendor pitches: sandboxing for AI agents, runtime access control for agents and APIs, and an all-source threat intelligence platform.

episodes.title: Vulnpocalypse Continues Until Defense Improves - PSW #950
episodes.summary: A long news round-up: patch cadence at Cisco and Fortinet, AI-found vulnerabilities, PHP exploitation still hitting firewalls, uncoordinated disclosure, new UK rules for undersea infrastructure and a DHS ban on DeepSeek.

episodes.title: A leak in the chain of command.
episodes.summary: A major DHS data leak, new research into Volt Typhoon's methods, a patched Cisco firewall zero-day, an attack on GitHub repositories, NIST post-quantum guidance and an actively exploited VMware ESXi flaw. Interview on securing operational technology in critical infrastructure.

episodes.title: How the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Works
episodes.summary: How a ten-person team ships at scale with an always-on fleet of AI agents, and what other businesses can learn; plus AI market headlines.
